brief.summary: Two GDACS advisories and recent news agree that Cyclone Remal, an Orange-alert storm, is heading for the northern Bay of Bengal coast near the Bangladesh–West Bengal border, with landfall estimated about 26 hours out on the evening of 26 May (UTC). Only two advisories are available, the timing moved by about 5 hours between them, and there are no river forecasts, so confidence is moderate rather than high.

reasons.text: Both advisories take the storm north into the northern Bay of Bengal, and the computed landfall is near 21.8N 89.16E in the Sundarbans area about 25.7 hours after the latest advisory.
The track moved about 41 km west between advisories, which is a normal adjustment but still enough to change whether the Khulna side or the West Bengal side of the border takes the core.
The estimated arrival time moved by about 5.1 hours between only two advisories, which is too short a record to call the forecast stable.

GDACS lists an Orange alert with 102 km/h winds for Bangladesh, India and Bhutan, which supports a damaging storm, though these are final reprocessed values and may not match what was shown at the time.

News independently tracks the system's development and a West Bengal alert, although an earlier headline warned that the landing point was unpredictable; river data is limited to low past readings, with no forecast to show flood risk.
